title: Rounded Fourier coefficient identity
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, $k\ge 0$, and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. Suppose the function on $\mathbb F_2^n$ given by $x\mapsto f(x)$ under the coordinatewise identification of the binary cube with the sign cube has at most $2^{k+1}$ nonzero Fourier coefficients. For any finite family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and any $U\in\mathcal F$, form the empirical Fourier hypothesis on $\mathcal F$ from the values of $f$ on the specified deterministic small-bias samples, then round each coefficient to the nearest multiple of $2(1/2)^{k+1}$. The rounded coefficient at $U$ equals the real Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by $U$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
the binary-cube Fourier sparsity of the transported function is at most $2^{k+1}$
$\mathcal F$ is a finite family of coordinate subsets
